demo.prompt: Audit the share images in this folder, and also the share image of https://vercel.com/ and of our skills site. Tell me what's wrong with them.
demo.result:
One table with a measured result per image, then each failure with its number and its fix. Three of its thirteen rows:

| Image or page | Size | File | Square crop | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| saassy-board.png | 622×326, too small | 115 KB PNG | logo cut: "Board"; headline cut on both sides | FAIL |
| vercel.com og:image | 2400×1350, 1.78:1 | 827 KB PNG | ok: nothing cut, but a logo with no words | FAIL |
| the skills site | no image | no image | no image | FAIL |

For the page with no image it named the cause from the site's source: the layout sets `openGraph` with no `images`, and the skill pages set their own `openGraph`, so each needs its own image.
demo.caption: Real output, shortened. 10 files and 2 pages, about 4 minutes.

before.label: Same request, no skill
before.text:
- A design critique per image: what reads, what is too small, what is cluttered.
- Found the missing image on the skills site and that the layout references none, and that Vercel's files are 16:9 and about 0.8 MB.
- Tried the square crop on Vercel's image only, not on the ten files.
- No fixed limits and no pass or fail per check, so two audits would not be comparable.
- Free-form report: prose per site and a verdict per file, in an order of its own.
before.note: A good critique. It also raised things the skill does not check, such as missing alt text and a missing og:url.

after.label: With og-image-audit
after.text:
- Every image measured against the same limits, with the number in each finding: 1200×630, 1.91:1, 300 KB.
- The square crop checked on every image: six of the ten files have text cut by it, quoted as it would read ("Board", "gelog", "Aft").
- Says which line of the site's source leaves the image out, and that the skill pages need their own.
- One table, then failures, warnings, review items and what was not checked.
- Says the files are captures, so their size may not be the real image's.
after.note: It judges crops and limits, not taste. For a design critique, the unaided review said more.

method: One run each, same request, same model (Claude Fable 5.2) and same tools, November 2026. The files were screenshots of share cards collected for research, plus two live pages.
